title: Bend statecharts for agent work · Hapsland layers
scope: Three Bend control-plane loops. Loop 3 snapshot tapes derive from the integration inventory; guard probes are what-if, never invented historical deployments. Runtime/build SHA gaps remain unverified.
trustBoundary: Bend decides every next state. The adapter only converts JSON to Bend constructors and back, and labels an unchanged state with the guarding law from this file. A replay is not an authorization, an admission or verified success, and it does not observe any live host.

availability.description: Kevin's self-reported availability (ROLES-v0): an owner action while Off is held in the needs-Kevin queue (L7).

limit.description: Supervision limit in minutes (the report used 2 h).

work-item.title: Proposed
work-item.summary: Someone wrote down a piece of work. Nobody owns it yet.

work-item.title: Claimed
work-item.summary: A coding lane (Opus or Sol only) took it. That actor becomes the author.

work-item.title: Implementing
work-item.summary: The author is writing code and pushing commits; the head SHA moves.

work-item.title: Verifying
work-item.summary: The author submitted. A CI actor who is not the author checks a receipt bound to this exact head.

work-item.title: DraftPR
work-item.summary: A passing receipt for the head opened a draft PR.

work-item.title: Integrated
work-item.summary: Ci or Opus (not the author) landed it on an integration branch with a passing receipt for that head.

work-item.title: Deployed
work-item.summary: The running service serves exactly the integrated head. The item now waits in the batched needs-Kevin queue.

work-item.title: OwnerAccepted
work-item.summary: Kevin (the owner, never the author) looked at the deployed result and said yes.

work-item.title: Merged
work-item.summary: Ci or the owner merged to the default branch, carrying the owner's acceptance.

work-item.title: Blocked
work-item.summary: Stuck on something outside the work. Only the owner or Opus unblocks or abandons.

work-item.title: Interrupted
work-item.summary: The worker died or was stopped. Its pushed head is kept; only Resume or an explicit Abandon moves it.

work-item.title: Abandoned
work-item.summary: An explicit decision by the owner or Opus to drop the work.

worker.title: Dispatched
worker.summary: A delegated worker exists but has not started on a host yet.

worker.title: Running
worker.summary: Working on a host and sending heartbeats.

worker.title: Stalled
worker.summary: No heartbeat for longer than the limit. One more limit of silence and it counts as interrupted.

worker.title: Interrupted
worker.summary: The worker stopped mid-task. A successor must resume it from its log, or someone abandons it explicitly.

worker.title: Overdue
worker.summary: Interrupted for longer than the limit with no decision. It sits in the needs-Kevin queue instead of vanishing.

worker.title: Completed
worker.summary: Finished. Its background processes must be reaped before it can be integrated or dropped.

worker.title: Resumed
worker.summary: A successor read the log and took the work (and its background processes) over.

worker.title: Abandoned
worker.summary: Dropped on purpose, with no background process left running.

worker.title: Integrated
worker.summary: Its result landed, with no background process left running.

lease.title: Lease free
lease.summary: No session owns this worktree/branch (or the S25 install lock).

lease.title: Lease held
lease.summary: Exactly one session owns it. Only the holder writes or releases; a takeover needs Reclaim with evidence the holder is dead.

device.title: Foreground unknown
device.summary: Nobody holds the install lock and nobody has looked at the screen since the last input.

device.title: Foreground seen
device.summary: Someone just looked: the foreground app is known, so one input may go to that app.

device.title: Foreground unknown
device.summary: A worker holds the install lock; the screen has not been looked at since the last input.

device.title: Foreground seen
device.summary: Lock held and the foreground app is known.

integration.title: Deployed
integration.summary: Exact running/build SHA equals integration head; checkout HEAD alone is insufficient.

integration.title: Parked
integration.summary: Explicit reason + future expiry in the head-bound decision record. Expiry requeues.

integration.title: Conflicted
integration.summary: Repair in isolation, re-test, then requeue.

laws.name: No merge without owner acceptance
laws.text: Merged is reachable only from OwnerAccepted, and that acceptance came from the owner, who is not the author.
laws.prevents: Agents (which act under Kevin's GitHub account) merging to main before Kevin has seen the deployed result.

incidents.label: PRs merged with no recorded owner acceptance of a deployed head

laws.name: No self-approval
laws.text: Verify (Ci), Integrate (Ci or Opus) and Accept (owner) are each passed only by an actor of the right role who is not the author.
laws.prevents: An agent grading or landing its own work.

incidents.label: integrations by the author's own account (indeterminate: agents share the owner's GitHub identity)

laws.name: Receipt bound to the head
laws.text: A draft PR needs a passing test receipt for exactly the head SHA; integration needs one for the integration head.
laws.prevents: "Tests passed" on an older commit being used to land a newer one.

incidents.label: integrated while the head had no passing receipt

laws.name: Deployed == integrated
laws.text: Deploy succeeds only when the service serves exactly the integrated head; observing any other head takes "deployed" away.
laws.prevents: The stale-service bug: a service quietly running an old or diverged build.

incidents.label: services stale (1), diverged (1) or missing merged commits (4)

laws.name: Interrupted is never dropped
laws.text: Interrupted leaves only by Resume (a coder takes the pushed head over) or an explicit Abandon by the owner or Opus.
laws.prevents: Half-done work silently disappearing when a worker dies.

incidents.label: interrupted items with no resume, PR or abandon decision

laws.name: Free models never implement
laws.text: Only Opus or Sol can claim or resume work; free models, Jev, SLMs and chat apps pick, rank and advise.
laws.prevents: Code written by a lane the owner ruled out for code.

incidents.label: no free-model claims seen; the model makes them unreachable

laws.name: Owner is a batched queue, not a blocker
laws.text: While Kevin is Off, an owner action is held and the item waits in the needs-Kevin queue; everything else keeps moving.
laws.prevents: Pinging Kevin outside a deep-work block, or one owner decision freezing other work.

incidents.label: items in the needs-Kevin queue at report time (availability: off)

laws.name: One owner per worktree
laws.text: A held lease passes on only by Reclaim with evidence the holder is dead; only the holder writes or releases.
laws.prevents: Two sessions editing the same worktree or branch at once.

incidents.label: writes by a second session while another held the worktree (19 worktrees)

laws.name: Resume from the log, or decide, within 2 h
laws.text: An interrupted worker is resumed from its log or explicitly abandoned; past the limit it turns Overdue (needs Kevin).
laws.prevents: Successors restarting blind, and interrupted workers rotting unnoticed.

incidents.label: 26 interrupted past the 2 h limit + 10 resumed without reading the log

laws.name: Reap or adopt background processes
laws.text: A worker reaches Abandoned or Integrated only with zero background processes; Resume hands them to the successor.
laws.prevents: Orphaned servers and jobs eating groot's memory after their owner died.

incidents.label: orphaned process still alive (plus 21 children reaped by Hermes, result lost)

laws.name: Heavy work off groot
laws.text: Heavy work starts on groot only with a declared GPU or toolchain exception; otherwise it runs on the MBP or a phone.
laws.prevents: Builds starving the memory-tight desktop and killing other workers.

incidents.label: heavy commands on groot with no exception (97 since the fleet came online; 1,310 excepted)

laws.name: Phone installs serialized
laws.text: Only the holder of the S25 install lock may install.
laws.prevents: Two agents installing builds over each other on the owner's phone.

incidents.label: of 17 S25 installs ran outside the lock

laws.name: Look before you tap
laws.text: Input goes only to the app last seen in the foreground, and each input spends that look.
laws.prevents: Taps landing in whatever app Kevin happens to have open.

incidents.label: of 23 S25 inputs sent with no foreground check

laws.name: Draft deadline
laws.text: Within 24 h: contained or explicitly parked, with reason and expiry. Unknown branch is an evidence gap, not verified non-containment.
laws.prevents: Within 24 h: contained or explicitly parked, with reason and expiry. Unknown branch is an evidence gap, not verified non-containment.

incidents.label: findings / evidence gaps (not all proven violations)

laws.name: Runtime equals integration
laws.text: Exact served/build SHA must equal integration head. Stale checkouts and unattested runtimes stay red.
laws.prevents: Exact served/build SHA must equal integration head. Stale checkouts and unattested runtimes stay red.

incidents.label: findings / evidence gaps (not all proven violations)

laws.name: One leased integration owner
laws.text: One unexpired per-repository lease. An active holder cannot be displaced.
laws.prevents: One unexpired per-repository lease. An active holder cannot be displaced.

incidents.label: findings / evidence gaps (not all proven violations)

laws.name: Consistent stacked chains
laws.text: A child's recorded base must contain its parent's current head.
laws.prevents: A child's recorded base must contain its parent's current head.

incidents.label: findings / evidence gaps (not all proven violations)

laws.name: Owner accepts before merge
laws.text: Only OwnerAccepted reaches Merged. Agents never approve their own work.
laws.prevents: Only OwnerAccepted reaches Merged. Agents never approve their own work.

incidents.label: findings / evidence gaps (not all proven violations)

planes.title: Loop 1 · Work item
planes.summary: One piece of work from proposal to merge. Draft PR kvnloo/z0intelligence#183.

planes.title: Loop 2 · Worker
planes.summary: One delegated agent from dispatch to an honest ending. Draft PR kvnloo/z0intelligence#184.

planes.title: Loop 2 · Shared resources
planes.summary: The worktree lease (also the S25 install lock) and the owner's phone.

roles.note: Taste, credentials, physical world, irreversible approvals. Attention is the bottleneck: one batched needs-Kevin queue.
Design, verification, hard code, orchestration. May claim, integrate, unblock, abandon.
Bulk well-specified coding. May claim and resume.
Advice and specs; no sandbox, no origin actions.
Scans, triage, summaries. Never code (owner rule, L6).
Fast chooser among prevalidated options; never writes.
CI, tests, service-branch checks, replay. Verifies and integrates; never the author.

explainer.intro: Three small Bend control-plane loops, drawn as layers. Every guard probe runs the same compiled Bend model.
loops: Loop 1 follows one piece of work: Proposed → Claimed (Opus or Sol only) → Implementing → Verifying (CI, not the author, checks a receipt for that exact commit) → Draft PR → Integrated → Deployed (the service must run exactly that commit) → OwnerAccepted (only Kevin) → Merged. Blocked, Interrupted and Abandoned are the side exits.

Loop 2 follows one delegated agent: Dispatched → Running (heartbeats) → Completed → Integrated. If it goes quiet it Stalls, then counts as Interrupted; a successor must resume from its log, or someone abandons it once its background processes are reaped. Past 2 h with no decision it turns Overdue and lands in Kevin's queue instead of vanishing. Beside it: one owner per worktree (the lease) and the S25 rules (install lock, look before you tap).

Loop 3 follows integration ownership: Branch → DraftPR → Queued → OnIntegrationBranch → Deployed → OwnerAccepted → Merged. Parked needs a reason and expiry. Conflicted needs repair. Snapshot tapes are evidence-backed what-if probes, not historical action logs.
explainer.statechart: This is poteto's statechart idea with Bend standing in for TLA+: draw the flow, write the laws, let the prover check the model, then replay real history through it to find where reality broke the rules. Here the laws are proven theorems about the same code that runs in this page, and the reports supply the incident counts.
explainer.roles: The guards are ROLES-v0 in code: only Opus/Sol write code, CI and Opus land work but never their own, Kevin alone accepts and is treated as a batched queue, free models/Jev/SLMs pick and rank but never implement.
